READABILITY.evidence: Section headers help, but the business logic is full of cryptic short names: `c`, `k`, `cf`, `cp`, `cy`, `lf`, `ss`, `ds`, `sf`, `df`, `rb`, `np`, `pk`. Helpers such as `rowp`/`rowpm` and `ceilShr(...)` usages have no comments explaining what they do.

MAINTAINABILITY.evidence: kernels.zig is 1495 lines and main.zig is 726, so the >500-line cap applies. The kernel families do share helpers. The `.zig-cache` and a 3.5 MB `zig-out/.so` are committed in the diff. `processGeneric` has duplicated chroma row-setup blocks.

ROBUSTNESS.evidence: createImpl validates formats, sizes and algo and returns null on error. But it uses magic bounds (`src_fmt > 9`, `algo > 2`). Missing planes silently fall back to `p0`/`q0`. Negative strides go through `@intCast` to usize, which is undefined behaviour in ReleaseFast.

C6-07-CASE1.evidence: Every plane is addressed through `rowp(p, y, stride)`. The special paths are guarded by parity checks (`dst_h & 1`, `dst_w & 1`), and odd chroma sizes are rounded up with `(w+1)/2`. 482 extra conversions (odd, tiny and non-multiple-of-16 sizes) were bit-exact against the reference. Bad configurations return null.

C6-07-CASE2.evidence: Exactly three `export fn` (swscale_create/process/destroy) with C ABI. process returns 0 on success and -1 on a null handle. Setup happens in create, the x86-64-v3 target is set in build.zig, and there are no threads.
